homestead.title: HOMESTEAD: Retro-Web Redesign Engine
homestead.tagline: Analyze any modern website and rebuild it the way GeoCities, FrontPage, or MySpace would have.
homestead.naming_note: GeoCities members were called Homesteaders. The framework borrows the word for the act of moving a modern site into an old neighborhood.

parameters.gif_min_frame_delay_basis: House budget. Two-frame full-contrast alternation reaches the WCAG 2.3.1 three-flashes-per-second line at roughly 167 ms per frame; HOMESTEAD doubles that margin. Tier: INFERENCE from claim C-021.
parameters.gif_tiny_delay_basis: Frames declared at 0 or 1 centisecond are treated as 100 ms, matching common browser clamping. Tier: INFERENCE, verify per browser.
parameters.large_animation_area_basis: WCAG 2.3.1 understanding text uses a 341 x 256 rectangle at 1024 x 768 as the 10 degree visual field estimate. Tier: STATED, claim C-021.
parameters.marquee_note: Marquee still renders in current browsers but needs a pause mechanism under WCAG 2.2.2. The Safe Mode toggle is that mechanism.

asset_policies.originals-only: Every image, sound, and font reference is generated by HOMESTEAD tooling or commissioned new. Default for client work.
asset_policies.archive-allowed: Generic archived glyphs (bullets, rules, construction signs) may be used for portfolio or commentary work, each logged with its source URL. Never recognizable third-party characters.

presets.rule: Each preset is a locked spec. Mixing elements across presets is allowed only when the era spec declares time_capsule true and names the story (for example a 1998 site last updated in 2006).

presets.name: Proto-Web / Academic
presets.host_context: University or ISP home directory, for example /~username/

canvas.note: Unstyled single column that simply wraps at the window edge.

presets.palette_note: Gray default background is UNCORROBORATED (C-030). Exact default link hex values are INFERENCE.
presets.layout: h1, paragraphs, hr, bullet lists, address footer. No tables for layout, no background images.
presets.nav_style: Inline text links and a Back to Home link at the foot of each page.
presets.voice: Dry and first-person. Pages describe themselves.
easter_eggs: Last modified date in the footer
forbidden_elements: CSS of any kind beyond the safety layer

presets.name: GeoCities / Angelfire / Tripod personal homepage
presets.host_context: Free homestead in a themed neighborhood, for example SiliconValley/Heights/4021

canvas.note: 600 to 620 px content for 1996 to 1998, 760 px for 1999 to 2000. INFERENCE from C-001.

presets.palette_note: Flat colors snap to the 216 web-safe cube (C-003). Photos use an adaptive palette GIF or a low-quality JPEG (C-004).
presets.layout: Centered column via the center element. Tables after about 1997. Framesets were common and are emulated, never used.
presets.nav_style: Text links separated by pipes at top and bottom, plus a few button GIFs.
presets.voice: Exuberant, personal, generous with exclamation points and capital letters.
voice_examples: This page is under construction, come back soon!
easter_eggs: Neighborhood address that matches the topic
Last updated date that is slightly stale
A generic Best viewed at 800x600 badge

presets.name: FrontPage / Dreamweaver small-business and corporate
presets.host_context: Company domain on a host with server extensions

canvas.note: Fixed table of about 760 px centered on a patterned background. INFERENCE from C-002.

presets.palette_note: Theme-driven. Flat art web-safe, photos adaptive. HOMESTEAD ships original look-alike themes, never Microsoft theme files.
presets.layout: Top, left, and bottom shared borders around a nested table body. Image maps for banners. Frames emulated if the concept calls for them.
presets.nav_style: Left shared border with beveled theme buttons and hover image swaps, plus a text link row in the bottom border.
presets.voice: Small-business formal with a hint of brochure.
voice_examples: Please send comments to our Webmaster.
This page was last updated on
easter_eggs: A [Hit Counter] placeholder where extensions are missing

presets.name: Web 1.5 portal / Y2K corporate

canvas.note: Three-column table at 760 to 780 px. INFERENCE from C-002.

presets.palette_note: Fuller color with glossy gradients rendered as GIF images, silver and blue tech accents.
presets.layout: Three-column tables, dense link rails, tabbed navigation GIFs.
presets.nav_style: Tab GIF row across the top and a dense left link rail.
voice_examples: Click here to make us your home page
easter_eggs: Make this my home page link
Weather box for a default city

presets.name: MySpace profile / Xanga / LiveJournal
presets.host_context: A profile on a social network with user CSS pasted into About Me

canvas.note: Default profile tables at about 800 px. INFERENCE.

presets.palette_note: Full color, black and pink and neon. Glitter is the marker of this era, not stars (C-024).
presets.layout: Fixed two-column default profile template with a gaudy user CSS block layered on top. Keep the skeleton visible underneath.
presets.nav_style: A thin network nav bar across the top, then profile sections. Links live in About Me.
presets.voice: Teen-confessional, decorated punctuation, inside jokes. Never quote real song lyrics.

mapping.rule: Translate component by component, not page by page. Every inventoried pattern gets a row decision: map, merge, or drop with a reason.
mapping.detect_note: Signals are case-insensitive regular expressions run by tools/survey.py. html signals match raw markup, text signals match visible text, href signals match link targets, script signals match script sources and inline script, css signals match style blocks and linked same-origin stylesheets.

verdicts.FINDINGS: At least one error-severity finding. The build does not pass.
verdicts.WARNINGS ONLY: No errors, at least one warning. Review every warning before scoring.
verdicts.NO FINDINGS (INCONCLUSIVE): No rule fired. Lint cannot judge visual authenticity, copy quality, or flash luminance, so absence of findings is never a clean bill. Score the rubric.

scopes.html: Raw HTML with comments stripped unless the rule says otherwise.
scopes.css: CSS files, style blocks, and style attributes.

rules.title: Web font loaded
rules.message: Web fonts are an anachronism and the Core fonts were never licensed for embedding.
rules.fix: Use a system font stack from canon/fonts.json. Never self-host Comic Sans.

rules.title: Rounded corners
rules.message: border-radius reads as post-2010.
rules.fix: Draw rounded shapes as GIF corner images or drop them.

rules.title: Blurred box shadow
rules.message: box-shadow is a modern tell.
rules.fix: Bake shadows into GIFs or use a table cell of a darker color.

rules.title: CSS gradient
rules.message: CSS gradients arrived long after these eras.
rules.fix: Render gradients into a tiled GIF.

rules.title: Flexbox or grid layout
rules.message: Flex and grid produce even gutters that read as modern.
rules.fix: Use table layouts with cellpadding, cellspacing, and spacer GIFs.

rules.title: Emoji character
rules.message: Emoji did not exist on the period web.
rules.fix: Use GIF smileys or ASCII such as :-)

rules.title: SVG or responsive image markup
rules.message: Vector and resolution-switching images are modern tells.
rules.fix: Export GIF or low-quality JPEG at a single small size.

rules.title: Responsive media query
rules.message: Period pages did not reflow. A 1998 page scrolls sideways on a phone.
rules.fix: Remove breakpoints. Offer a scaled view in the delivery wrapper if needed.

rules.title: Modern icon set
rules.message: Modern icon sets break the era and carry their own licenses.
rules.fix: Generate pixel glyphs with tools/gifsmith.py.

rules.title: Modern framework fingerprint
rules.message: View Source shows a modern framework.
rules.fix: Hand-write period markup. Only the safety layer may be modern.

rules.title: Modern marketing copy
rules.pattern: \b(get started|book a demo|we use cookies|accept all cookies|sign in with google|ai-powered|supercharge|seamless(ly)?|level up|unlock your|scroll down|swipe)\b
rules.message: Copy uses a modern marketing pattern.
rules.fix: Rewrite in the preset voice from canon/presets.json.

rules.title: Autoplaying audio
rules.message: Audio that starts on its own fails WCAG 1.4.2 and browser autoplay policy.
rules.fix: Use the safety layer click-to-play control (data-hs-audio). Keep any bgsound line inside an HTML comment for View Source flavor.

rules.title: Blink without the safety layer
rules.message: blink does nothing in current browsers and needs a pause mechanism when emulated.
rules.fix: Link homestead-safe.css, which animates blink at one cycle per second and stops it in Safe Mode.

rules.title: Marquee without the safety layer
rules.message: Auto-moving text over five seconds needs a pause mechanism (WCAG 2.2.2).
rules.fix: Link homestead-safe.js, whose Safe Mode stops every marquee.

rules.title: Safety layer missing
rules.message: Every HTML page must link homestead-safe.css and homestead-safe.js.
rules.fix: Copy kits/safety-layer next to the build and link both files in the head.

rules.title: Real frameset
rules.message: Real framesets break deep links, accessibility, and mobile.
rules.fix: Emulate frames with tables or iframes inside a fixed layout.

rules.title: Java applet
rules.message: Applets no longer run.
rules.fix: Rebuild hover buttons and banner rotators as image swaps. A gray applet-loading box may stay as flavor.

rules.title: Flash file reference
rules.message: Flash has been blocked since January 2021.
rules.fix: Build the intro in HTML and CSS on a 550 by 400 stage, or ship an original SWF through Ruffle.

rules.title: Image without alt text
rules.message: Images need alt text. Spacer GIFs take alt="".
rules.fix: Add alt text. Period-style alt such as [Under Construction] is fine.

rules.title: Flat color off the web-safe palette
rules.message: Flat colors in presets A to C should sit on the 216 web-safe cube.
rules.fix: Run tools/websafe.py snap and record the before and after in the asset log.

rules.title: Required widget missing
rules.message: A widget the preset requires is not marked anywhere in the build.
rules.fix: Add the widget and its <!-- hs:widget ID --> marker, or record why it was dropped in the mapping worksheet.

rules.title: Era mixing
rules.message: A widget from another preset appears in this build.
rules.fix: Remove it, or set time_capsule true in the era spec and explain the story.

rules.title: Canvas width off era
rules.message: The outer layout table is missing a fixed width or uses one outside the era tolerance.
rules.fix: Set the outer table width to the preset canvas width within 40 px.

rules.title: Modern CSS feature
rules.message: Custom properties, rem and viewport units, and modern functions are tells.
rules.fix: Use px, attributes, and plain CSS1 or CSS2 declarations.

rules.title: Modern image format
rules.message: WebP and AVIF are modern formats.
rules.fix: Use GIF or JPEG.

rules.title: Modern loading attributes
rules.message: Lazy loading and fetch hints show up in View Source.
rules.fix: Remove them; period pages are small.

rules.title: Modern CDN
rules.message: Modern CDN references show up in View Source.
rules.fix: Ship files next to the page.

rules.title: Motion budget exceeded
rules.message: Animated GIFs, marquees, and blinks on the page exceed the preset motion budget.
rules.fix: Cut motion or move items below the fold. Budgets live in canon/presets.json.

fonts.policy: Reference installed system fonts through font-family stacks or the font face attribute. Never use @font-face for presets A to E. The Core fonts were never licensed for web embedding (C-031) and Comic Sans webfont licensing is sold separately (C-032).

stacks.C: Book Antiqua, Times New Roman, serif

process.core_principle: A retro redesign is a translation, not a costume. Lock one era, inventory the modern site, map every component to its period equivalent, build in period markup, then let a separate auditor grade it.

phases.name: Intake
phases.question: What are we redesigning, for whom, and under what rights?
steps: Capture the target URL or saved HTML
Record purpose: client, portfolio, commentary, or internal
Record audience and deliverable: static mock, live site, screenshots, or video
Choose the asset policy: originals-only or archive-allowed
Note legal context: own brand, client brand, or third-party brand

phases.name: Site survey
phases.question: What does the modern site actually contain?
steps: Fetch the top page and up to ten same-origin pages
Extract navigation, information architecture, headings, CTAs, forms, embeds, and scripts
Extract brand colors and font families from markup and stylesheets
Detect modern patterns against canon/mapping.json signals
Capture tone of voice notes and screenshot references

phases.name: Era lock
phases.question: Which single era will this site live in?
steps: Recommend a preset from purpose, brand, and audience
Set year, browser, canvas width, palette mode, fonts, and layout mode
Copy required widgets and forbidden elements from the preset
Set motion budget, audio mode, and easter eggs
Pull two or three reference pages from the archives for the preset
Decide whether a time capsule story is intended and write it down

phases.name: Component mapping
phases.question: What does each modern component become?
steps: Generate the mapping worksheet from the inventory and era spec
Decide map, merge, or drop for every detected pattern
Cap navigation at five to eight items and plan the sitemap
Plan lived-in details
Write the era copy deck in the preset voice

phases.name: Asset sourcing and generation
phases.question: What images, colors, and sounds does the build need, and are we allowed to use them?
steps: Snap brand colors to the web-safe cube and log the deltas
Rebuild the logo as a WordArt-style or beveled GIF
Downscale and dither photos
Generate buttons, badges, counters, rules, tiles, and glitter with original tooling
Render the click-to-play track
Log every asset with source, license, and era check

phases.name: Build
phases.question: Does the page look and read like it was made then, and behave safely now?
steps: Start from the preset kit and the safety layer
Write period markup at the canvas width
Place every mapped component and widget marker
Wire Safe Mode, click-to-play audio, and the text-only page
Lint after every file and fix errors before moving on

phases.name: Authenticity and safety QA
phases.question: Would a 1998 visitor believe it, and is it safe for a 2026 visitor?
steps: Run the anachronism lint against the era spec
Run the GIF timing audit
Score the 40-point rubric without reading the builder's notes
Check View Source, the text-only page, and keyboard paths
Check the asset log and legal notes
Issue SHIP, REVISE, or REBUILD with rows to fix

agents.pattern: CADRE: one orchestrator session over tool-isolated subagents. The orchestrator owns the engagement folder, sequencing, and human checkpoints. Subagents own one phase each and hand back a contract, not a conversation.

agents.name: site-surveyor
agents.contract: inventory.json valid against schemas/inventory.schema.json plus notes.md

agents.name: era-archivist
agents.contract: era spec valid against schemas/era-spec.schema.json with two or more reference URLs

agents.name: component-mapper
agents.contract: every detected pattern has a map, merge, or drop decision; copy deck passes HL011

agents.name: asset-smith
agents.contract: every file in images is in the asset log with source, license, and era check

agents.name: authenticity-auditor
agents.writes: nothing; returns the scorecard JSON and notes to the orchestrator
agents.contract: complete 20-row scorecard with evidence per row and a verdict from tools/rubric.py

tiers.VERIFIED: Checked directly against a primary artifact by the maintainer.
tiers.CORROBORATED: Two or more independent sources agree.
tiers.STATED: A single credible source states it.
tiers.UNCORROBORATED: Only a weak, secondary, or retrospective source supports it, or sources disagree.
tiers.INFERENCE: HOMESTEAD reasoning built on the cited claims. Treat as design guidance, not fact.

sources.provenance_note: Claims were compiled from a November 2026 research pass (REF HOMESTEAD-001). No claim is marked VERIFIED because no primary artifact was re-checked at build time. Promote a claim only with a commit that records what was checked.

claims.claim: In January 2000 W3Schools logged 800x600 at 56 percent of visitors, 1024x768 at 25 percent, and lower resolutions at 15 percent; 12 percent still ran 256 colors. The audience skews toward developers, so treat these as an upper bound on screen size.
By January 2004 W3Schools logged 1024x768 at 47 percent and 800x600 at 37 percent.
The 216 web-safe colors are every combination of 00, 33, 66, 99, CC, and FF across red, green, and blue, shipped for 8-bit displays where the operating system reserved 40 colors.
Period guidance held that the browser-safe palette suits flat illustrations and logos but should not be used to remap color photographs.
Only 22 of the 216 web-safe colors displayed reliably on 16-bit screens (Lehn and Stern). HOMESTEAD does not ship that sub-palette until the list is checked against the primary source.
The marquee element is obsolete in the HTML specification but still implemented by current browsers.
The blink element does nothing in current browsers. Firefox, the last browser to blink, removed it in version 23 (2013); it maps to HTMLUnknownElement.
Adobe ended Flash Player support on December 31, 2020 and blocked Flash content from January 12, 2021.

The research pass reported that frameset documents are no longer supported. This conflicts with the HTML standard still describing frameset rendering. HOMESTEAD emulates frames for linkability, accessibility, and mobile reasons regardless of browser support.
GeoCities was founded in November 1994 by David Bohnett and John Rezner as Beverly Hills Internet and from mid-1995 gave Homesteaders free pages of 2 MB in themed neighborhoods.
Neighborhood names were part of the page address. Examples include Area51, Athens, BourbonStreet, Broadway, CapitolHill, Hollywood, Paris, Petsburgh, and SiliconValley.
Yahoo acquired GeoCities on January 28, 1999, announced closure on April 23, 2009, and ended the United States service on October 26, 2009.
There were over 38 million GeoCities pages when the United States service shut down.
The amateur web of the 1990s is catalogued by starry tiled backgrounds, animated Under Construction signs, rainbow rules, Mail Me envelopes, MIDI background music, and collections of animated GIFs.
FrontPage 98 shipped named themes including Arcs, Artsy, Automotive, Barcode, Bars, Blends, Blocks, Blueprint, Bubbles, Cactus, Expedition, and Sumi Painting.
Microsoft announced FrontPage 2000 with 10 new business-ready themes among more than 60 professionally designed themes.

FrontPage components included Annotation, Categories, Confirmation Field, Discussion, Hit Counter, Include, Registration, Save Results, Scheduled Image, Scheduled Include, Search, Substitution, Table of Contents, Timestamp, and Validation.
Shared borders lived in _borders, hover buttons and the banner ad manager were Java applets kept in _fpclass, and the hit counter needed server extensions on the host.
Experienced FrontPage users of the period advised against Java hover buttons because visitors without a Java VM saw no buttons, and recommended image swaps instead.
MySpace allowed HTML but not JavaScript in profile fields, so layouts were CSS blocks pasted into About Me that restyled the default tables.
WCAG 2.3.1 forbids more than three flashes in any one second unless below thresholds, and estimates the 10 degree visual field as a 341 x 256 pixel rectangle at 1024 x 768.
WCAG 1.4.2 requires a pause, stop, or volume mechanism for any audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds.
MySpace began testing the drag-and-drop Profile 2.0 editor in October 2008 and rolled it out optionally in November 2008.
In the later profile-based amateur web, glitter replaced stars as the signature decoration.
Top Friends was originally limited to eight and later allowed between 4 and 24, while the name Top 8 stuck.
MySpace peaked in the United States at 75.9 million monthly unique visitors in December 2008 (comScore).
GifCities indexes over 4.5 million GeoCities GIFs, launched in 2016, and gained semantic search and size filters in June 2025.
The 1996 Space Jam website remains online and is the canonical surviving studio site of the era.
Neocities launched on June 28, 2013 and passed one million sites on February 10, 2025.
Early browsers rendered unstyled pages on a gray background close to C0C0C0. Source is research synthesis only.
The Core fonts for the Web were redistributable only in their original installer packages and were never licensed for web embedding.
Comic Sans webfont licensing is sold separately.
An existing agent skill converts a landing page into a FrontPage 97, 98, or 2000 style site with themes and components.
web98 uses a language model to render any address as if it were 1996. Useful for ideation, prone to invented period details.
A 2021 concept set reimagined popular apps as 1990s websites as static mockups.
98.css recreates Windows 98 interface chrome from semantic HTML without JavaScript. It styles operating system chrome, not web pages.
Cameron's World is a 2015 web collage of GIFs and text from archived GeoCities pages.
One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age posts screenshots of restored GeoCities pages rendered in period browsers.
Profile layout generators exposed background color and image, tiling, font family and size, text and link colors, table background, and border width, style, and color.
A profile carried About Me, Who I'd Like to Meet, Interests, a Details table, a contact table, a friends grid, and a comments wall.
Design to 600 to 620 px of content for 1996 to 1998 and 760 px for 1999 to 2003.
Period markup with a thin modern safety layer passes View Source scrutiny and leaks fewer spacing and typography tells than a modern framework styled to look old.
A minimum frame delay of 340 ms for animated GIFs keeps two-frame alternation at about half the WCAG flash limit.

rules: Terminal Navy canvas, BH Blue accents, hairlines not boxes, square corners, no drop shadows, no gradients on motifs.
One BHIL motif per figure: the dot constellation only on HS-01, the ASCII pipeline only on HS-03, the prompt chevron in the eyebrow everywhere else.
Retro specimens (pixel type, bevels, badges, counters, period colors) sit inside the BHIL frame as content, never as the frame.
Every animation is CSS, slow, small in area, stops under prefers-reduced-motion, and frame zero is the designed static frame.
No em dashes or en dashes; the repository dash gate scans every SVG.
